articles.title: Shingles Vaccine Linked to Lower Heart Attack and Stroke Risk, Major Studies Find
articles.excerpt: A study published in Nature found the newer shingles vaccine reduced cardiovascular burden by 9% over seven years, adding to earlier research showing vaccinated heart patients were 46% less likely to suffer a serious cardiac event.
articles.image_caption: A healthcare worker administers a vaccine to a senior patient. Multiple studies have now linked the shingles vaccine to significantly lower cardiovascular risk.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face disproportionately higher cardiovascular disease rates, making the shingles vaccine's newly discovered heart benefits especially relevant for Indian American adults over 50.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi H1N1 Cases Cross 2,600 as Hospitals Scale Up Isolation Wards
articles.excerpt: India's capital has recorded around 3,000 influenza cases this year, with H1N1 accounting for nearly three-quarters of all Influenza A infections. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has called an emergency review meeting.
articles.nri_angle: Health advisory for NRIs and Indian Americans planning travel to Delhi during the monsoon season amid a sixfold surge in H1N1 influenza cases.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Women With Type 2 Diabetes Face Higher Mental Health Risk Than Men, UK Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A study of nearly 29,000 UK patients reveals that women are 53% more likely to develop mental health conditions after a type 2 diabetes diagnosis, while men face higher cardiovascular and kidney risks.
articles.nri_angle: Type 2 diabetes is disproportionately prevalent in South Asian populations, making sex-specific care insights especially relevant for the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Scientists Develop RK-251, a Smart Cancer Drug That Activates Only Inside Tumour Cells
articles.excerpt: Researchers at IASST and IIT Guwahati have created a drug candidate that uses cancer cells' own chemistry to trigger its anticancer payload, potentially reducing chemotherapy's collateral damage.
articles.image_caption: A researcher works in a laboratory setting. Indian scientists at IASST and IIT Guwahati have developed RK-251, a drug candidate designed to activate only inside cancer cells.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin researchers and diaspora families following cancer treatment advances will note this contribution from Indian institutions to global oncology research, with potential implications for treatment access in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Landmark Trial Shows 4 in 5 Rectal Cancer Patients Can Avoid Major Surgery
articles.excerpt: The STAR-TREC trial, published in The Lancet Oncology, found that chemoradiotherapy allowed most early-stage rectal cancer patients to keep their rectum and skip radical surgery.
articles.image_caption: A radiotherapy machine in a hospital clinical setting. The STAR-TREC trial found that chemoradiotherapy can allow most early-stage rectal cancer patients to avoid radical surgery.
articles.nri_angle: Colorectal cancer incidence is rising among Indian and South Asian populations globally, making advances in less invasive treatment options directly relevant to diaspora families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Doctors Urge Early Action on Malaria and Dengue as India's Monsoon Season Peaks
articles.excerpt: Health experts warn that dismissing early symptoms as routine viral fever is the most common and dangerous mistake during monsoon months, when all Indian states except Ladakh are endemic to mosquito-borne diseases.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs planning monsoon-season visits to India should be aware of malaria and dengue warning signs and consult travel health specialists before departure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Woman Develops Severe Brain Disorder After 15-Day Water-Only Diet, May Never Walk Normally Again
articles.excerpt: Doctors diagnose Wernicke's encephalopathy after a Chinese woman's extreme fast depleted her vitamin B1 reserves, leaving her with a 'penguin-like' gait that may be permanent.
articles.image_caption: Wernicke's encephalopathy, a severe brain disorder caused by vitamin B1 deficiency. A 31-year-old woman developed the condition after a 15-day water-only fast.
articles.nri_angle: Extreme fasting trends, including practices rooted in traditional Eastern medicine, have gained popularity globally; the case serves as a health warning for communities where prolonged fasting is culturally practiced.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: PM2.5 Pollution Linked to Millions of Cancer Cases Beyond the Lungs, Nature Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A sweeping analysis across 952 global locations ties long-term fine particle exposure to cancers of the breast, digestive tract, and liver — with South Asia bearing a disproportionate burden.
articles.image_caption: Airborne particulate pollution. A major study in Nature links PM2.5 exposure to millions of cancer cases beyond the lungs, affecting multiple organ systems.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cities face some of the world’s worst PM2.5 levels, making this study directly relevant to families in India and diaspora members concerned about relatives’ health.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Australian Baby First in World to Receive Precision Treatment for Rare Epilepsy
articles.excerpt: Eight-month-old Bodhi went from 50 seizures a day to virtually none within weeks, while Indian doctors advance VNS therapy for drug-resistant cases.
articles.image_caption: An Australian infant has become the first in the world to receive a precision gene therapy treatment for a rare form of epilepsy.
articles.nri_angle: Indian doctors at CARE Hospitals Hyderabad are advancing VNS therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy, highlighting India’s growing capacity in neurological care.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Twenty Minutes of Exercise Works as Well as a Nap to Rescue a Sleep-Deprived Brain
articles.excerpt: A McGill University study finds both a short workout and a 90-minute nap boost memory by 22% after 30 hours without sleep — but through different brain pathways.
articles.image_caption: New research finds that just 20 minutes of exercise can restore cognitive function as effectively as a nap for sleep-deprived individuals.
articles.nri_angle: Sleep deprivation is a widespread concern for diaspora professionals and shift workers; the study offers a practical intervention accessible to anyone with 20 minutes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HPV Vaccine Cuts Risk of Head, Neck, and Other Cancers, Studies Show
articles.excerpt: New research finds the vaccine protects against cancers well beyond the cervix, with vaccinated men and boys nearly 50% less likely to develop several HPV-related malignancies.
articles.image_caption: A vial of HPV vaccine. New studies show the vaccine significantly reduces the risk of head, neck, and other cancers beyond cervical cancer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Old Blood Accelerated Alzheimer's in Mice, Reviving Debate Over Transfusion Risk
articles.excerpt: Animal studies show Alzheimer's-linked proteins can travel through blood, but the largest human studies on whether transfusions raise dementia risk reach opposite conclusions.
articles.image_caption: A brain scan comparison showing Alzheimer's disease progression. A new study found that old blood accelerated Alzheimer's pathology in mice.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six Free, Evidence-Backed Daily Habits That May Add Years to Your Life
articles.excerpt: Forget expensive supplements and longevity hacks — decades of research point to simple, everyday practices as the most reliable path to a longer, healthier life.
articles.image_caption: A person cycling outdoors. Research identifies six daily habits, including regular exercise and quality sleep, that may add years to your life.

sources.label: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

articles.nri_angle: Many longevity habits align with traditional South Asian practices — plant-based diets, multigenerational households, yoga, and community gatherings

articles.title: Six Warning Signs That Overtraining Is Undermining Your Fitness Goals
articles.excerpt: From persistent fatigue to declining performance, exercise science experts explain how too much training can do more harm than good — and what to do about it.
articles.nri_angle: For fitness-conscious Indian Americans balancing demanding work schedules with gym routines, recognizing overtraining signs can prevent injuries and burnout.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Research Links Lead Exposure to Deeper Neuronal Damage Through Inflammatory Pathways
articles.excerpt: A peer-reviewed study identifies the gene networks through which lead poisons brain cells, reinforcing calls for stricter environmental controls in India and globally.
articles.image_caption: New research has found that lead exposure triggers neuronal damage through inflammatory pathways, deepening understanding of how even low-level exposure can harm brain function.
articles.nri_angle: With millions of Indian children exposed to lead above WHO thresholds, the research underscores an environmental health crisis that remains largely invisible to the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala's Shigella Outbreak Exposes Growing Threat of Drug-Resistant Infections
articles.excerpt: With 226 cases and six deaths this year, Kerala's recurring shigellosis outbreaks mirror a global surge in antibiotic-resistant Shigella strains that health authorities are struggling to treat.
articles.nri_angle: Kerala's recurring shigellosis outbreaks are a reminder for NRIs traveling to India during monsoon season to exercise caution with water and food safety.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wash Rice Twice: UK Drought Campaign Targets South Asian Cooking Habits Amid Water Emergency
articles.excerpt: England's water authorities are asking South Asian households to cut rice-washing from seven times to two and urging Muslims to reduce ablution water as more than half the country sits in drought.
articles.image_caption: A UK drought campaign is urging South Asian households to limit rice washing to two rinses as water reservoirs drop to critical levels across southern England.
articles.nri_angle: UK water campaigns directly target South Asian cooking and Muslim religious practices, raising questions about how conservation burdens are distributed among diaspora communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Diet Plans Look Convincing but Miss the Mark on Calories and Nutrition
articles.excerpt: New research reveals AI-generated meal plans undercount calories by nearly 700 per day, while photo-based tracking apps miss up to 345 calories per meal.
articles.image_caption: A study found that AI-generated diet plans from tools like ChatGPT frequently miss calorie targets and overlook key nutritional needs.
articles.nri_angle: AI tools trained on Western dietary patterns may poorly estimate calories and macronutrients in Indian meals rich in ghee, oils, and complex spice preparations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: What Is Ferritin Face? The Viral Trend That May Signal Hidden Iron Deficiency
articles.excerpt: A TikTok trend linking pale skin and dark under-eye circles to low iron stores has gone viral — and doctors say there is a kernel of truth worth paying attention to.
articles.image_caption: Low ferritin levels can cause visible changes including dark circles, pale skin, and thinning hair, prompting the viral 'ferritin face' trend.
articles.nri_angle: Iron deficiency disproportionately affects women on vegetarian and plant-based diets common in Indian diaspora households, making this trend particularly relevant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Kriti Sanon Swears By Daily Fibre and Electrolytes Over Just Protein
articles.excerpt: The Bollywood star and wellness investor says most people overlook fibre — but nutritionists warn her approach needs context.
articles.image_caption: Bollywood actor Kriti Sanon at a promotional event. Sanon has spoken about prioritizing fibre and electrolytes as part of her daily nutrition routine.
articles.nri_angle: Bollywood wellness trends resonate with health-conscious diaspora audiences; practical nutrition advice applicable globally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Visible Signs Your Body Is Getting Better at Handling Insulin
articles.excerpt: A shrinking waistline and fading dark skin patches may signal your insulin sensitivity is improving, even before blood tests catch up.
articles.image_caption: An illustration depicting insulin sensitivity and metabolic health markers. Doctors say visible changes in skin and waistline can signal improving insulin function before lab results shift.
articles.nri_angle: Relevant for health-conscious diaspora readers tracking metabolic wellness markers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Doctors Sound Alarm on Antibiotic Overuse as India's Monsoon Drives Surge in Resistant Infections
articles.excerpt: A Bhaskar investigation found antibiotics routinely prescribed for common colds and fevers without diagnostic tests, as experts warn India may be entering a 'post-antibiotic era.'
articles.nri_angle: Returning NRIs and travelers to India face elevated risks from drug-resistant infections during monsoon visits, while antibiotic stewardship practices common abroad remain weakly enforced across Indian hospitals and pharmacies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV Declares Family the 'First School of Humanity' in Sweeping AI Encyclical
articles.excerpt: The pontiff's 83-page teaching document 'Magnifica Humanitas' calls for an educational alliance to protect human dignity in the age of artificial intelligence.
articles.nri_angle: The encyclical's call for AI regulation and its emphasis on family-centered education resonate with Indian diaspora parents navigating their children's growing dependence on digital technology.
